sections.h2: Which Wayne County office sends the bill, and which one collects late tax?
sections.html:
Each city and township in Wayne County prepares its own assessment and tax rolls and mails July and December bills from its own treasurer. The county treasurer steps in only for delinquent real property, at 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, in Detroit.

A separate unit, the Assessment and Equalization Division of the Department of Management and Budget at 500 Griswold, Suite 2650, advises the County Commission on equalizing local values and apportioning taxes. Call (313) 967-0010 or write equalization@waynecountymi.gov for the Parcel Viewer GIS app. The division also offers annual assessment data, historical GIS parcel shape files and old tax maps for download at no cost. Detroit has its own assessor at (313) 224-3035 and a City Treasurer property tax division at (313) 224-3560.

For a current bill, anywhere in the county, start with the treasurer of the city or township where the house stands.

sections.h2: When does Wayne County treat property tax as delinquent?
sections.html:
The cutoff is the end of February. Tax not paid to the local treasurer by then turns delinquent on March 1, and only the Wayne County Treasurer takes payment afterward. The county participates in the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund program, and every community and school district is in it. Detroit joined starting with tax year 2003.

The county's tax information line is (313) 224-5990. Delinquent accounts can be paid online. A bank debit is free, while Visa, MasterCard and American Express add a 2.49 percent fee that goes to the processor. Partial payments are welcome by mail or in person, and a receipt requires a stamped, self-addressed envelope or an online request.

County staff say they have no authority to waive penalties and interest or to shrink a bill after it is issued, because the state expects each taxpayer to pay on time. Cutting future bills is a job for exemptions, which the local assessor decides.

sections.h2: What is the forfeiture and foreclosure schedule in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Public Act 123 of 1999, codified at MCL 211.78, shortened the road to tax foreclosure from roughly five years to roughly two. The county's timeline page walks through each stage, and the table condenses it.

Stages of tax forfeiture and foreclosure for Wayne County parcels
StageTreasurer's description
First March 1 after the bill yearUnpaid taxes are delinquent and go to the county treasurer, with a 4% administration fee and 1% interest per month
October 1A $15 collection fee is added to each parcel
Following March 1The property is forfeited; $175 and $30 recording fees are added, and interest rises to 1.5% a month back to the first delinquency date
AutumnNotices of the show cause and judicial foreclosure hearings are served on an occupant or posted on the property
WinterRemote show cause hearings in January, then judicial foreclosure hearings in February
March 31Last day to redeem by paying taxes, interest, penalties and fees
April 1Foreclosure takes effect and title passes to the county treasurer
September and OctoberPublic auction of foreclosed parcels

Before any foreclosure, the treasurer reports at least ten contacts: four first class letters, three certified ones, a personal visit and two occupant mailings.

sections.h2: What relief does the Wayne County Treasurer offer before foreclosure?
sections.html:
Payment plans and a hardship extension are the two main tools. The extension is open to owners who hold title by recorded deed or land contract, occupy the home as a principal residence and face a substantial financial hardship. The income yardstick is 125 percent of the Federal Poverty Level, but owners slightly above it are told to apply anyway.

  • Bring photo ID from Michigan, the deed, proof you live there such as a utility bill, and proof of income.
  • The Taxpayer Assistance staff reply within 30 days once the application is complete.
  • Applications come from the treasurer's page, by phone at (313) 224-5990, or at the office by appointment.
  • Title trouble can go to United Community Housing Coalition, (313) 963-3310, or the Legal Aid and Defender Association, (313) 964-4130.

A poverty exemption that can trim or erase future bills is requested through the local assessing unit. Lenders sometimes miss tax payments after a refinance, so match your mortgage statements against the local treasurer's records.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Wayne County house that has tax owing?
sections.html:
Yes, provided the tax is paid by closing. A warranty deed has to carry county treasurer certificates reporting no tax liens and five prior years of paid taxes, per MCL 211.135, while a quitclaim without warranty covenants is excused.

For deed certification the county treasurer charges $5.00 per document covering up to 25 parcel numbers, plus 20 cents for each additional parcel. Only originals qualify. Mail them with a check or money order to Wayne County Treasurer, Deed Certification, 400 Monroe St., 5th Floor, Detroit, MI 48226, enclosing a stamped return envelope, or bring them to an appointment. The certified deed then goes to the Register of Deeds, which requires its own appointment for recording.

When a parcel is already forfeited, payment remains possible until the following March, and interest keeps building monthly. Paying off the balance from sale proceeds beats waiting for foreclosure.

sections.h2: How do appeals and county equalization fit together in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Appeals start locally, at the city or township Board of Review and then the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Anyone who received a change through either one is told to ask the local assessor's office or the Tribunal for an explanation.

Equalization is a second look at the totals. Under MCL 211.30a, every local unit delivers its roll to the county equalization division by the Wednesday following the first Monday in April. The Board of Commissioners convenes the Tuesday after the second Monday in April and must finish by the first Monday in May under MCL 211.34. The aim is to spread the countywide tax burden evenly among cities and townships.

sections.h2: What happens to a foreclosed Wayne County property?
sections.html:
State and local governments get first refusal on a foreclosed parcel at the minimum bid. Whatever they pass over goes to public auction in September and October of the foreclosure year, opening at the delinquent taxes, penalties and interest. Winners receive a quit claim deed, and every sale is "as is" and "where is".

Former owners may still recover leftover money. MCL 211.78t lets a person who held title or equity at foreclosure claim any proceeds above the debt, starting with a notarized notice of intent delivered by July 1 after the foreclosure. The treasurer answers by January 31, and a circuit court motion can follow between February 1 and May 15.

sections.h2: What is Wayne County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Wayne County was formed in 1796 as the sixth county of the Northwest Territory and named for General Anthony Wayne. It then covered the whole Lower Peninsula and bits of four other states. Today it spans 673 square miles, 9 percent of it water along the Detroit River and Lake St. Clair, and it is the most populous county in Michigan, with 1,769,038 residents in the 2025 estimate. Detroit is the seat. Dearborn, Livonia, Westland, Taylor, Wyandotte and the Grosse Pointes are also here, and the southern communities are called Downriver. Detroit Metropolitan Airport is in Romulus.

The Census Bureau counts 700,591 households, 64.8 percent owner-occupied, with a median home value of $178,500, a median income of $60,539 and median rent of $1,132. About 2,931 people live per square mile. Values vary by community, so the local assessor's record carries more weight than a countywide figure.

faqs.q: When do Wayne County property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. Tax not paid to the local city or township treasurer by the end of February is delinquent from the next March 1 and can be paid only at the Wayne County Treasurer's Office.

faqs.q: How long before Wayne County can foreclose for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: About two years. One year of delinquency leads to forfeiture the next March 1, and foreclosure follows a year later unless taxes, interest and fees are paid by the March 31 deadline.

faqs.q: Can the Wayne County Treasurer reduce my tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Once taxes are billed the county cannot reduce them or waive interest and fees. Exemptions that lower future bills are requested from your local assessing unit.

faqs.q: What does Wayne County charge to certify a deed for taxes?
faqs.a: $5.00 per document covering up to 25 parcel numbers, plus 20 cents per added parcel. Only original documents can be certified.

faqs.q: Can I get money back if my Wayne County home sold at foreclosure auction?
faqs.a: Possibly. Owners with title or equity at foreclosure may file a notarized notice of intent to claim surplus proceeds by July 1 after the foreclosure. A court motion follows only if proceeds remain.
